# #295 — P1: Inventory and automatically migrate legacy lanes to exact scope

Parent: #293

## Problem
Legacy session lanes can occupy the same namespace + session_key as the new exact-scope runtime while carrying incompatible agent, platform/source, server, channel, or thread coordinates. Migration is manual and incomplete: dev:open-brain was repaired, while dev:Development still caused online PostCompact writes to spool.

## Required behavior
Provide a safe, idempotent migration system that preserves lane history without crossing exact-scope boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria
- Read-only inventory classifies exact, legacy, conflicting, duplicate, orphaned, and already-migrated lanes.
- Dry-run produces an explicit migration plan with before/after content-free receipts.
- Migration supports resumability, interruption recovery, collision detection, and rollback.
- Preserve the valid distinction between Development/dev:Development and open-brain/dev:open-brain.
- Never merge or relabel lanes across namespaces or exact scopes because repositories are nested or names are similar.
- Define alias/tombstone behavior so retired legacy coordinates cannot continue receiving writes.
- On first direct startup/write, safely establish missing coordinates or return an actionable migration-required result before spooling or split history.
- Tests cover repeated migration, mixed populations, collisions, interrupted migration, rollback, cross-namespace rejection, and nullable thread identity.

## Security
Namespace and all seven scope coordinates remain server-enforced security boundaries.
